question: The nucleophilic substitution reactions of halogenated derivatives can proceed through a bimolecular (SN2) or unimolecular (SN1) mechanism. Which of the following characteristics is applicable to the SN1 reaction ?:

options.opb: The kinetics of the reaction depends on the concentration of the nucleophilic species.
options.opc: Carbocations are formed as intermediate species.
options.opd: Fluorinated aliphatic compounds are more reactive than the corresponding chlorinated derivatives.

reasoning_chain: CHAIN: SN1 reaction -> proceeds through a unimolecular mechanism -> 80% CHAIN: SN1 reaction -> involves the formation of carbocations as intermediate species -> 90% CHAIN: SN1 reaction -> does not involve a concerted process -> 70% CHAIN: SN1 reaction -> the kinetics of the reaction depends on the concentration of the nucleophilic species -> 80%
analysis: In SN1 reactions, the nucleophilic substitution proceeds through a two-step mechanism involving the formation of a carbocation intermediate. This makes option 'opc' applicable to the SN1 reaction.
